newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Talks on to free foreign hostages on Nigerian rig.
newsitem.headline: Talks on to free foreign hostages on Nigerian rig.

text.p: Negotiations have started to try to free 20 foreigners, mostly Frenchmen, held hostage on an oil rig by Nigerian workers, a spokesman for the company they work for said on Thursday.
"This problem started yesterday morning and we are working hard to resolve it," said Ben Shibo, the spokesman for French oil contracting firm ETPM in Lagos.
"Everything should hopefully be under control by the end of the day, by the grace of God," he added but declined to say why the foreigners were taken hostage.
In Paris a French foreign ministry spokesman said the French embassy in Lagos had mobilised and was in contact with both the local authorities and ETPM.
The 16 Frenchmen and four other Westerners are being held on the rig situated in the Escravos area near the coast of Warri in the oil-producing Delta state in midwestern Nigeria.
Chevron Corp's Nigerian joint venture is the biggest oil operator in Escravos and a spokesman for the company said they were checking on the incident but had no immediate information.
It is the second such hostage-taking by local people in the last four months.
Twenty-eight foreigners including 10 Fillipinos and nine Frenchmen were held on a barge operated by ETPM about 30 miles offshore last Christmas by 60 Nigerian workers demanding higher wages.
Apart from being deprived of food for two of the five days they were held captive on the barge, the hostages were not harmed.
"We have these kinds of problems all the time with local communities and it really is not as serious as it is taken," said Shibo.
